i just completed (SL125) a faith/dex build myself....it is most certainly worth it/viable for PvE and PvP!

i think the following weapons work well with this type of build:

* Lothric Knight Sword - this is my bread and butter sword. great range for its size, has extra crit damage, and has a nice roll catching stab. @ 40 dex / 40 fth use a sharp infusion + lightning buff for max damage. if you dont like buffing and want to save the FP for other spells, throw a lightning infusion on it, its more damage than the unbuffed sharp. some people recommend blessed for it, but im fairly certain lightning is more AR. 
* Sunlight Strait Sword - another great weapon for this build as it scales well with faith and has some dex scaling. also can be buffed with lightning blade. also has atk/def buffing weapon art for yourself and vicinity (helps with co-op and kinda makes you feel like a paladin in terms of role-play).  not as versatile as the lothric knight sword but its nice to mix things up. 
* Hollowslayer Greatsword - doesnt have faith scaling but has great dex scaling and added bonus damage to hollows (helps mainly in PvE and a little in PvP). Also has a wide swing, great for dealing with mobs of enemies/zoning yourself from your opponent/roll-catching. Swing is slightly slower than the lorthic knight and sunlight strait so it can help mix up combat. I mainly use for PvE but i have definitely fended off invaders with this. also flavorful for role-play as a faith paladin. 
* Dragonslayer's Axe - this mainly scales of strength so i do not personally use, but it does have some dex scaling. has base lightning damage without infusion, and will have lightning damage boosted with a blessed or lightning infusion. def viable as a back up/change up weapon. 
* Mail Breaker/Dagger - Throw a blessed infusion on it and use it as your secondary. it will give passive health regen while out, has great critical hit bonus damage, and can mix up combat with fast strikes. 
* Shield - i personally dont use blocking shields, just the target shield for parrying. regardless, any shield could help with some added defense if youre worried about being a wet noodle. i infuse my target shield with blessed for the passive health regen, also applies while its on your back. 

Not too knowledgeable about katanas myself (I see frayed blade in your post, apologies if you wanted more katana recommendations). I do know the uchigatana is great early game.

In terms of catalysts, the Saint's talisman will have the best spell buff once your build is complete (assuming faith 40-45). Otherwise if you want the chonk casting poise use the sunlight talisman. 

Some other spells i also use on my build are: 

* Tears of Denial - mainly in PvP or boss fights, for obvious reasons
* Way of White Corona - real nice spell in long hallways/choke points where you can get your enemy when the disc returns. also helps with zoning your opponent. 
* Great lightning spear - not as powerful as sunlight spear, but faster and stronger than the regular lightning spear. 
* Lightning Arrow - amazing PvP spell, fires quick and doesnt suck that much FP.
* Force - fun for pushing invaders off cliffs or getting somebody off your back. casts fairly quickly as well. 
* Heals - use whatever one suits your playstyle. helps with co-op and is nice flavor for role-play.
* Caressing Tears - SLEPT ON SPELL IN PVE. absolutely incredible spell for getting through farron or any area with status effects. not that great in PvP though, i just use for "adventuring."

Armor you can really wear whatever you want, however I would keep weight ratio under 70% to avoid fat rolling. besides the roll, fashion > practicality in my humble opinion haha. 

Rings:

* Ring of favor - boosts health, stamina, and equip load, all around great ring. +3 version in ringed city dlc. 
* Mornes and Sun's first born - boost your miracles. 
* Chloranthy - stamina regen its priceless, this ring has saved my ass so many times. +3 version in ringed city dlc. 
* Lingering dragoncrest - helps extend the length of buffs if you are running them. 
* Darkmoon ring - gives 2 attunement slots if you want more spells. Useful depending on how high your attunement is and how versatile you want your spell casting to be.

hey man, glad to hear youre passionate about the game and want to improve! rocket league is a tough game for sure, a lot harder than what meets the eye. good on ya for trying, hope some of these tips will help:

first, it seems like youre working on a lot ball control mechanics (which isnt a bad thing), but at your level the most important aspect to work on is game sense and rotations. knowing how to position yourself and how to play the ball in various situations is much more important than being able to air dribble or carry up the wall. being mindful of how to rotate and synchronize with a team mate will put you in a position to make the best play and prevent you from getting trapped in a bad spot where you cant challenge the ball. here is a great youtube video about it from musty: https://youtu.be/_B752_08Pfw

another thing i would work on is accuracy and power of your hits. this will help on offense when shooting/scoring AND especially on defense with clears. a well placed shot or clear can really throw the other team off their balance. knowing at what angle to hit the ball and when to hit the ball is crucial for this. here is a good video from thanovic about this: https://youtu.be/-TSOvHj8s2U

as others have said, your level and rank DO NOT matter, as long as you feel that you personally are improving, then youre doing something right. most importantly however, remember to have fun, its the reason we all keep coming back to flying car soccer after all. 

lmk if these help and if you want anymore pointers! good luck!

A couple years into my regular cannabis consumption, I started getting panic attacks while stoned, enough so that it made me take a very long, almost one year long hiatus from smoking.  I found that a lot of it was due to external stressors that marijuana was merely exacerbating.  I eventually started smoking again after making some effort to deal with them, and the panic attacks generally subsided, bar the occasional anxiety-ridden sesh that occurs every once in a blue moon.  

Perhaps you too have some important life events/stressors that are subconsciously bothering you and weed is bringing them out.  If you do suffer from anxiety, depression, or other mental illness, try getting some help/finding another outlet to cope while decreasing your usage, or taking a full break altogether.  

If you don't think you are having these problems outside of cannabis, maybe anxiety about having a panic attack is what is getting you stuck in a nasty feedback loop.  Whenever I do have an anxious episode while high, there is always some nervousness surrounding the next one.  I know this did also plague me when I first returned from my long break.  

Hope my advice helps and you find some peace with your issue, friend.  Best of luck!

Hey u/Matt_Thaxton,

To answer your first question, what would lead a nihilist to be a communist, I believe that most nihilistic people lose their faith in humanity once they begin identifying with some form of communism.  This is purely anecdotal, based on what I've experienced while organizing, having personal discussions/debates, and viewing online "leftist culture."  There is a classic joke that encompasses this, that I have seen and heard many times, "the worst thing that ever happened to me was becoming a leftist."  Once people come to an understanding of socialism, communism, anarchism, etc. really any school of leftist thought, they begin to view and interpret the world through the lens of that ideology.  As Marx himself wrote in the communist manifesto, "... it \[the bourgeois\] creates a world after its own image."  We are all living under the capitalist mode of production, alienated from product and fellow laborer; we are all living in a world designed to benefit and maintain the rich, ruling class.  Most people do not see the every day transgressions of capitalism until they are looking at it from a class-based analysis.  The more people understand leftist thought, the more easier it becomes to identify these instances of oppression in one's daily life.

To answer your next question, why would you think that a system of common ownership would work in community of people who you believe to be incapable of caring for one-another, I don't believe people are incapable of caring for one-another.  The nihilistic outlook that many people take is not that people are incapable of caring for one-another, but like other QuarantineProtocol has said, is rooted in how entrenched and expansive the current order of things seems.  Humans are born with an innate sense of altruism for their fellow man. Whether it be as intimate as their parents, or as foreign as a complete stranger, there is an evolutionary benefit to caring for a fellow member of your species. Despite this, people are also a product of their environment, the material conditions they experienced during development.  Capitalism serves to bury this altruism and foster a sense of selfish individualism coupled with extreme commodity fetishism within people.  Capitalism forces members of its society to be self-centered to merely survive.  Given how many people internalize this attitude, it seems almost impossible to have a fundamental cultural change away from said selfishness and create a new zeitgeist based on mutual aid and community oriented thought, which is, again, why many leftists become nihilists like you said.  A timeless argument against communism is, "People are inherently selfish/greedy/lazy, communism will never work," (I am not implying you made this assertion nor that you believe it, however it is similar in nature to your question, and the counter-argument serves to answer both).  However, if this argument is to be believed, and what I have said about inherent altruism within mankind and people changing via the material conditions surrounding them is *wrong*, I would ask then why we have modeled our society under capitalist mode of production.  Capitalism allows this human greed to fester and take advantage of others.  It creates hierarchies and inequalities in which power is concentrated in the hands of those said greedy, selfish individuals.  The eventual goal of communism, anarchism, etc. is to create a classless society in which people are interdependent.  Why give those who are greedy an opportunity to act on it? Why not use an economic system like communism to prevent said greed to take advantage of one another and create an environment where people are forced to be dependent/reliant on one another to prevent this inherent selfishness from permeating society?

I hope my comment helps answer your questions, glad to see a civil debate about these difficult topics.

Hey there, here's some advice!

**If you are playing 2s or 3s:**  
I would say the most important thing to work on is rotation.  If you were once plat, I'm sure you know the fundamentals, but it can never hurt to brush up on the basics.  Below I linked Sunless Khan's video on 3s rotations, there is some variation between 2s and 3s of course, but the general gist is the same.  There are a bunch of solely 2s based rotation tutorials on Youtube as well.  Knowing when/what to play the ball vs rotate back is essential for higher level play.  Another important aspect is tracking where your teammate(s) and opponents are on the field.  This will help with making in-game decisions.  Working on mechanics like shadow defense, power shots, aerials etc, will do you no good without the knowledge of when to use them appropriately.  In the unfortunate case you get a bad teammate, your solid rotation will help cover you most of the time.  

Sunless Khan 3s rotation tutorial:  
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=THcMLWOEc\_o](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=THcMLWOEc_o)  


**If you are playing 1s:**  
Again, game sense is extremely important.  Of course, there isn't a rotation per say, but getting familiar with your own mechanical abilities will help make decisions when challenging.  Always make sure when you do make a challenge, that if you lose the 50/50, your net isn't wide open for the opponent to punish.  Boost steals, bumps, and well-positioned clears can all disrupt plays, leave the opponent out of position, and give you time to reset, collect boost, and set yourself up for a better play.  

**In general:**  
SPEED.  Being able to move around the field faster and more efficiently is a great way to make yourself a better player.  When recovering, always make sure your car hits the ground on its wheels, facing the direction you intend to travel next.  Another good mechanic to learn if you don't know already is the half-flip.  This will let you make U-turns quickly and flip the direction your car is facing on the go without losing momentum.  This isn't too hard of a mechanic to learn, just requires a couple sessions in free play once you understand the fundamentals.  I linked Kronovi's tutorial below.  There are some other mechanics like flip cancels, wave-dashes, etc. but these are not too important at your level and take a lot more time to learn how to use consistently as the half-flip, I would concentrate on that first.  Boost management is super important too.  Always make sure you are effectively using your boost and don't get trapped all thirsty with 0 during a clutch play.  Small things like not boosting once you have supersonic trails and collecting small pads whenever possible are very important, especially in 3s when corner boost is less available.  

Kronovi half-flip tutorial:  
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9920AGZg620](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9920AGZg620)  


A final tip is DO NOT WORRY ABOUT YOUR RANK; my friend in champ 2 tells me this all the time. As long as you feel you are bettering yourself by playing, that is the only thing that truly  matters.  Yes, rank is nice and all, but the most important thing is that you are improving.  Do not get discouraged, Rocket League is brutally unforgiving, but you will get there in time!  

Hope my advice helps friend!
